title: Indium-free transparent conductors
bottleneck: Touchscreens, solar cells, and displays depend on indium tin oxide, but indium is scarce, brittle, and price-volatile. Alternatives — silver nanowires, graphene, conductive polymers, doped zinc oxide — each fail on at least one axis: nanowires haze and corrode, polymers lack conductivity, and zinc oxide cannot match ITO's combination of transparency, conductivity, and process compatibility. No drop-in replacement has taken meaningful market share.
why_it_blocks: Indium supply risk threatens the cost trajectory of displays and thin-film solar, and ITO's brittleness blocks flexible electronics. Without a true replacement, the transparent conductor remains a single-point-of-failure material for the entire optoelectronics industry.
current_state: Silver nanowire films serve in some flexible touch sensors, and the industry keeps ITO viable through thinner coatings and recycling. But a universal, indium-free, flexible transparent conductor is still a materials goal, not a product.
